scenes.text: You've waited months for tonight.
scenes.visual: Candlelit path; you and your wife walking close, sleeves touching, she glances at you.

scenes.text: Your wife is right beside you. So is your mother. Your father. Three little brothers. And a grandmother who has never once slept.
scenes.visual: Family members pop into frame one by one; grandmother's wide unblinking eyes last.

scenes.text: One room. Eight people. And you need five minutes alone.
scenes.visual: Cutaway of a one-room house packed with sleeping bundles; you and your wife in the middle looking at the camera.

scenes.text: You have a plan. It's a bad plan. But it's a plan.
scenes.visual: You hold up a finger; your wife raises one eyebrow.

scenes.text: Plan A. The village walks you to bed. In some places, that's tradition: candles, songs, advice you did not ask for.
scenes.visual: Lantern procession to a doorway; guests crowd, one raises a finger, one thumbs up.

scenes.text: The last guest winks at you. You have never wanted to hurt a stranger so much.
scenes.visual: Wink close-up; your clenched fist, your wife patting it.

scenes.text: They finally go. Your wife looks at you. You look at her. Your mother clears her throat from the bench.
scenes.visual: Firelight on both faces; behind them mother on a bench, arms folded.

scenes.text: Plan A is dead.
scenes.visual: A big "A" crossed out, wobbling.

scenes.text: Plan B. "Let's get some air." Your wife takes your hand and you slip out into the dark field.
scenes.visual: Moonlit field, two figures running hand in hand, laughing.

scenes.text: It's quiet. It's cold. It's perfect. Then a lantern bobs up from the hedge. Then another. Then six.
scenes.visual: Wide field; one by one, lanterns rise from the grass, each over a couple.

scenes.text: Turns out you were not the first newlyweds to ask for some air. Somebody's cousin waves.
scenes.visual: A cousin waves from the hedge, a couple scrambling to straighten their clothes.

scenes.text: Plan B is dead. It's also freezing.
scenes.visual: You, shivering, scarf flapping; your wife blows into her hands.

scenes.text: Plan C is ambitious. The lord's manor. The rich had private rooms upstairs, with real beds and real curtains.
scenes.visual: Stone manor at night, a lit upper window, a canopy bed visible with curtains half drawn.

scenes.text: You tiptoe up the stairs. A soft bed. Heavy curtains. A door that shuts. And a very large man holding a lamp.
scenes.visual: Staircase; at the top a huge steward silhouette with a lamp, you two frozen mid-step.

scenes.text: "What are you doing in the lord's bedroom?" "Looking at curtains." Your wife nods like an expert.
scenes.visual: Steward looming; you pointing at the curtain; your wife nodding seriously.

scenes.text: You are removed by the collar. Curtains, it turns out, are for people who own the building.
scenes.visual: You and your wife tossed out the door in a heap; the door slams.

scenes.text: Plan C is dead.
scenes.visual: A big "C" crossed out.

scenes.text: Plan D. Wait. Everyone sleeps eventually.
scenes.visual: Back in the house, you and your wife sit up in the dark, watching the sleepers.

scenes.text: Your father snores. Your brothers sleep in a heap. Your mother finally turns away. And the grandmother's eyes glint in the dark.
scenes.visual: Dark room; sleeping bundles, and one pair of eyes lit by the embers.

scenes.text: Your wife leans in and whispers a question. What day is it? You tell her. Her face falls.
scenes.visual: Her lips at your ear, then both of you staring at a wall calendar.

scenes.text: A church tradition, going back centuries, frowned on couples being together on certain days. How strictly people kept it is debated. Your grandmother keeps it strictly. For everyone.
scenes.visual: Calendar with crosses; grandmother raises one eyebrow, still not asleep.

scenes.text: Plan D is dead. You're starting to feel like a guest in your own marriage.
scenes.visual: You, slumped, holding a cup; your wife patting your knee.

scenes.text: And that's when your wife says it. "Then stop looking for a room."
scenes.visual: Close on her, firelight on her face, a spark in her eyes.

scenes.text: Plan E. You build one.
scenes.visual: You roll up your sleeves; a pile of planks, a saw, a bad attitude.

scenes.text: Planks. A saw. Your wife holding the board, saying you're doing it wrong. A bed with four walls and a door on the front.
scenes.visual: Montage: you sawing, plank snaps, sawdust puffs, her hands over yours to steady the saw.

scenes.text: People really did this. A bed with walls and a door, a tiny house inside the house. They're called box beds.
scenes.visual: The finished box bed, plain wooden, door open, firelight inside.

scenes.text: You climb in. Your wife follows, laughing into her sleeve so nobody hears.
scenes.visual: Two figures squeezing into the box, her hand over her mouth, shoulders shaking.

scenes.text: It's small in there. Her shoulder against yours. Her breath an inch from your ear.
scenes.visual: Close, warm: two faces in firelight, nearly touching.

scenes.text: One inch of wood away, your father coughs. Your grandmother turns over, very pointedly.
scenes.visual: Wall cross-section: the two of you inside, family silhouettes outside, the grandmother's eye at a knothole.

scenes.text: So you learn the first rule of marriage in a one-room house. Quiet is a skill.
scenes.visual: Your wife presses a finger to your lips, eyes full of mischief.

scenes.text: She finds your hand in the dark. And you find out she's been practicing longer than you.
scenes.visual: Interlaced hands in a thin gold line of light.

scenes.text: You pull the door. It sticks. Then it shuts.
scenes.visual: Close on the box door swinging shut, hand on the latch. Nothing beyond it.

scenes.text: The firelight shrinks to one thin gold line. The house falls away.
scenes.visual: Outside view: house at night, lanterns going dark one by one, the box a faint glow.

scenes.text: For the first time all day, nobody is watching.
scenes.visual: The closed box door, warm light at the seams.

scenes.text: It wasn't much of a door.
scenes.visual: Slow push on wood grain and a crooked hinge.

scenes.text: It was the only one in the house, and you built it yourself.
scenes.visual: Same frame held; the scarf tail lifts in a draft. Fade to black.
